findings: Desktop entry project targets net8.0-windows even though README and native service dispatch also describe Linux. This explains the hardcoded net8.0-windows build-output path in linux_build.sh; Linux execution itself remains unqualified.

Native Windows project targets net8.0 with unsafe code enabled and System.Drawing.Common 10.0.8; platform restriction is expressed on relevant classes rather than the project target. Native Linux references the shared Avalonia-based service interface project.
Solution includes five projects and Debug/Release Any CPU configurations, but no test project. Existing JPEG harness is task-owned and does not constitute upstream application tests.

AppUpdater.deps.json lists AppUpdater 1.0.0 plus Semver 3.0.0 and Microsoft.Extensions.Primitives 5.0.1. It is metadata, not source; listed package SHA512 values have not been independently checked against artifacts.

Desktop sets source-revision inclusion false and version 3.2.0-preview. Application manifest contains historical AvaloniaTest.Desktop assembly name and Windows 10 compatibility declaration. No OS compatibility claim derived from these declarations.
